reader.requirement: At --std 85 every explicitly referenced nonunique user-defined name (data-name, record-name, condition-name with data-names, condition-names and record-names counted as one disjoint set, index-name, sum counter, file-qualified record items, clause operands such as OCCURS DEPENDING ON, RECORD KEY, SORT KEY and READ KEY) must be refused unless its qualifiers single out exactly one declaration; a reference whose qualifiers do reach exactly one must bind to it.

edition-consulted.switches: Year < 2002: condition-names, data-names and record-names are one disjoint set, so a level-88 and a data item of one tier reached by the same reference are counted together (COBOL-85 only)
counts the rival condition-names beside data items at 85; returns 0 at 2002+
counts the rival data items beside a level-88 at 85; returns 0 at 2002+

DialectLevel >= 2002: a data description clause operand (ODO DEPENDING ON, SAME AS, OCCURS KEY, RENAMES) takes the subject's groups as implicit qualifiers; at 85 every candidate of the scope is counted
ConstructRegistry qualified-index-name-2002 gate: a qualified index-name is refused at 85 (COBOL0900), as X.1.3.8.3 says index-names cannot be qualified
Edition.Cite chooses the 1985 or 2023 citation text only; the verdict is the same code
at 85 a level-88 and a data item may share a spelling (one disjoint set) instead of COBOL2692 at 2002+

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 a level-88 and a data item reached by one reference are one ambiguity (2023 refuses the declaration pair with COBOL2692); at 85 an ODO operand in the subject's own group is not implicitly qualified (2023 accepts s1-odo-same-group); at 85 an index-name cannot be qualified

reader.notes: Every class of nonunique reference probed is refused with COBOL1639 (COBOL2145 for sum counters) and every sufficiently qualified one binds to the right item at run time. Two citation texts are used for the one requirement (SRL2.1 in most binders, SR3 in UniqueOrReportAmbiguous, OdoResolvePass and RECORD KEY); both pass cite.py, so this is wording, not a defect.

refuter.evidence: Probes at --std 85 under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/reread-1985-fixed/out/refute-1985-f01/src/, each aimed past the reader's set. Refused with COBOL1639, as SRL2.1 requires: r1-01-vs-05 (01 X beside G.X, unqualified X), r1-self-name-ambig (01 D / 05 D, unqualified D), r1-call-using-ambig (CALL USING X), r1-write-rec-ambig (WRITE R, R in two FDs), r1-filestatus-ambig (FILE STATUS S), r1-relkey-ambig (RELATIVE KEY RK), r1-linage-ambig (LINAGE IS LN), r1-varying-ambig (RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON RL), r1-occkey-ambig (OCCURS ASCENDING KEY K unqualified with K in two tables; class c: 1985 has no implicit qualifier for clause operands, and VI.5.8.3 SR2 'Data-name-1 and data-name-2 may be qualified' gives the remedy), r1-rw-source-ambig / r1-rw-sum-ambig / r1-rw-control-ambig (report SOURCE, SUM addend, CONTROL operand), r1-cond-group-qual (K OF G reaching a level-88 and a data item: one disjoint set at 85).
